design_detail: Exploratory secondary analysis of the first phase 3 trial of MDMA-assisted therapy for severe PTSD (MAPP1; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03537014; 15 sites in the US, Canada and Israel; card sc_mitchell_2021): change in self-reported hazardous alcohol use (AUDIT) and drug use (DUDIT) from baseline, before randomization, to study termination, compared between MDMA with manualized therapy and inactive placebo with the same therapy, in the 82 of 90 participants with both assessments. Read as the accepted author manuscript in PubMed Central (NIHMS1847922), not the publisher's version. Sponsored and fully funded by MAPS; organized by MAPS PBC.
can_establish: Whether, within a randomized trial in people with severe PTSD and little current alcohol or drug problem, AUDIT and DUDIT scores changed differently with MDMA-assisted therapy than with placebo plus the same therapy over about 4 months.
cannot_establish: Whether MDMA-assisted therapy treats alcohol or other substance use disorders (no participant had a current alcohol use disorder and other current substance use disorders were excluded); whether consumption itself changed (the AUDIT and DUDIT are screening questionnaires, and their recall window was 12 months at baseline but only the time since treatment ended at termination); or longer-term substance use, including later MDMA use.

sample.recruitment: As in MAPP1 (card sc_mitchell_2021); participants recruited 7 November 2018 to 26 May 2020 (3.1 Sample characteristics, 1st paragraph).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Severe PTSD (CAPS-5 of 35 or more, symptoms for at least 6 months); psychiatric disorders and alcohol and substance use disorders in the last 12 months assessed with the MINI; current mild alcohol or cannabis use disorder, or moderate disorder in early remission for 3 months, allowed; any other substance use disorder within 12 months excluded; past disorders more than 12 months before allowed (2.2 Participants, 1st paragraph).
sample.demographics: Of the 82: 64.6% women; 80.3% White; mean age 41.4 (12.2); past alcohol use disorder 21 (25.6%) and no current one; past substance use disorder 14 (17.1%); current mild cannabis use disorder 2 (both on placebo); any alcohol use (AUDIT 1 or more) 69 (84.2%); any drug use (DUDIT 1 or more) 48 (58.5%); baseline CAPS-5 43.8 (6.0) (3.1 Sample characteristics, 2nd paragraph; Table 1).
sample.attrition: Three MDMA and 4 placebo participants withdrew; analyses use the 82 with both baseline and termination AUDIT or DUDIT (complete cases) (3.1 Sample characteristics, 1st paragraph).
sample.selection_effects: The trial population had little current alcohol or drug disorder: no participant with even a mild alcohol use disorder was recruited, although permitted (4. Discussion, 2nd paragraph); results say nothing about people with substance use disorders.

exposure.measurement: As in MAPP1: after medication taper, three 90-minute preparatory sessions, randomization, three 8-hour experimental sessions with MDMA or placebo, each followed by three 90-minute integration sessions over 3 to 4 weeks; participants, site staff and sponsor blinded until database lock (2.3 Intervention, 1st paragraph).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions as printed: in each of three sessions a divided dose, 80 mg plus 40 mg in the first session and 120 mg plus 60 mg in the second and third, the supplement 1.5 to 2 hours after the initial dose; supplements and the increase could be withheld or declined; placebo on the same schedule (2.3 Intervention, 1st paragraph).
exposure.polysubstance: The outcomes are the alcohol and drug-use questionnaires themselves; cannabis was the only drug with a permitted current (mild) disorder (2.2 Participants).

comparison.controls: Inactive placebo with the identical therapy (2.1 Study design; 2.3 Intervention).
comparison.matching: Randomized (MAPP1). In the 82 analysed, baseline AUDIT 4.26 (4.28) on MDMA vs 2.83 (3.27) on placebo (Table 1; text P = .10); the authors report no significant group differences at baseline.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Not applicable to a randomized comparison.

outcomes.instruments: AUDIT (10 items, 0 to 40; hazardous alcohol use) and DUDIT (11 items, 0 to 44; drug use and drug-related problems), self-reported at baseline with the standard 12-month lookback and at study termination with instructions altered to cover the time since the end of treatment; CAPS-5, adapted SDS, BDI-II and modified C-SSRS from the parent trial for correlations (2.4 Outcome measures, 1st paragraph).
outcomes.validity_norms: Screening instruments, not diagnostic, with cited validity across populations (2.4 Outcome measures).
outcomes.operationalization: Between-group difference in change scores from baseline to termination, by t test and models with and without adjustment for the baseline score; Hedges' g for significant effects; Pearson correlations of AUDIT change with CAPS-5, SDS and BDI-II (2.5 Statistical methods, 1st paragraph).
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None; two exploratory outcomes, each tested with and without baseline adjustment, plus correlations.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Self-report by participants who, in MAPP1, very probably knew their allocation (card sc_mitchell_2021); blinding of participants was not formally assessed in MAPP1.

analysis.effect_sizes: AUDIT change: −1.02 (SD 3.52) on MDMA vs +0.40 (2.70) on placebo, F printed as (80, 1) = 4.20, P = 0.0436, Hedges' g = 0.45; after adjustment for baseline AUDIT, P = 0.52. Within groups: MDMA 4.09 (4.16) at baseline and 3.24 (3.36) at termination (P = .30); placebo 2.80 (3.18) and 3.23 (3.65) (P = .57). DUDIT change: −1.36 (3.00) vs −0.78 (5.39), F printed as (80, 1) = 0.37, P = 0.5452, g = 0.13 with a printed 95% CI of 0.013 to 0.89; within groups MDMA 2.70 to 1.33 (P = .10), placebo 3.45 to 2.70 (P = .53). AUDIT change correlated with baseline CAPS-5 in the MDMA group only (r = .32, P = .04) (3.2 AUDIT and DUDIT scores, 1st paragraph; Abstract). Editors' calculation from the printed change means and SDs: difference 1.42 AUDIT points, t(80) = 2.04, g about 0.45, matching the printed F and g.
analysis.covariates: Baseline score in the adjusted models.
analysis.preregistration_detail: The parent trial is registered (NCT03537014); AUDIT and DUDIT were exploratory measures, not registered outcomes, and their results were not reported in the main trial paper (card sc_mitchell_2021). No analysis plan for this secondary analysis is cited.
analysis.selective_reporting: The abstract and highlights report only the unadjusted AUDIT result (P = 0.0436); the baseline-adjusted result (P = 0.52) appears only in the Results and Discussion.
analysis.power: No power calculation for these outcomes; the authors note that the narrow distribution of AUDIT scores limited the ability to detect change (4. Discussion, 2nd paragraph).

interpretation_gap.results_show: In 82 people with severe PTSD and no current alcohol use disorder, AUDIT scores fell by 1.0 point on MDMA and rose by 0.4 on placebo (on a 0 to 40 scale); the difference was significant without adjustment but not after adjusting for the MDMA group's higher baseline (P = 0.52). DUDIT changes did not differ. The termination questionnaires covered only the period since treatment ended, against 12 months at baseline.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract says MDMA-assisted therapy was associated with a "significantly greater reduction" in AUDIT change scores, without the adjusted result, and concludes that it may lead to subclinical improvements in alcohol use and does not appear to increase the risk of illicit drug use (Abstract). The highlights speak of greater decreases in alcohol consumption, which the AUDIT does not measure directly. The Discussion says the reduction in alcohol use may be uniquely associated with MDMA-assisted therapy and that the protocol did not show an increased risk of substance use, abuse or dependence, or of MDMA use, during and 2 months after treatment (4. Discussion, 1st and 4th paragraphs); MDMA use is not reported separately in the paper, and the supporting long-term follow-up it cites (Jerome et al., 2020) is marked retracted in PMC. The Discussion acknowledges that the adjusted effect was not significant and that the sample without alcohol use disorder limits interpretation (4. Discussion, 1st and 2nd paragraphs).

timeline.event: MAPP1 main report (Mitchell et al.); AUDIT and DUDIT were exploratory and not reported there.

replication.where_it_stands: A single exploratory analysis; the authors announce long-term follow-up data on AUDIT, DUDIT and MDMA craving and use (4. Discussion, 4th paragraph), not among the sources read. The MAPP1 card records, from the registry, a 'substance use' adverse event in 3 of 46 MDMA and 0 of 44 placebo participants, which this paper does not mention.

funding.funder: MAPS sponsored the trial, provided the MDMA and fully funded it from private and foundation donations; MAPS PBC, its wholly owned subsidiary, organized the trial (Acknowledgments; Role of funding sources).
funding.declared_conflicts: As printed: JBW, AC and AE received salary support for full-time employment with MAPS PBC; BY-K and RD for full-time employment with MAPS; CRN, JM and SK received funding from MAPS PBC during this and other studies; CRN is also paid for contract work as an MDMA-assisted therapy trainer (Declaration of Competing Interest).
funding.affiliations_note: A sponsor employee (JBW) carried out the statistical analysis; sponsor staff oversaw data collection (CRediT statement).

what_would_settle_it: A randomized trial of MDMA-assisted therapy in people with PTSD and a current alcohol use disorder, with consumption measured by timeline follow-back over equal windows and verified biologically, blinded raters and follow-up of at least 12 months, reporting any later MDMA or other drug use.

domains.note: Central randomization in MAPP1 (card sc_mitchell_2021); the higher baseline AUDIT on MDMA (P = .10) is compatible with chance.
As in MAPP1: participants probably aware of allocation through drug effects; the analysis concerns the effect of assignment among those with data.
Eight of 90 (9%) excluded as incomplete, complete-case only; reasons for withdrawal could relate to substance use.
Self-reported questionnaires by participants who probably knew their allocation, and a recall window that changed from 12 months to the period since treatment ended between the two measurements.
Unregistered exploratory outcomes; the unadjusted and baseline-adjusted analyses disagree (P = 0.0436 and 0.52) and the abstract reports only the significant one.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: Randomized, but the outcomes are exploratory self-reports with a changed recall window in a largely unblinded trial, and the reported effect depends on the choice between two analyses. The paper can be cited for the small size of the AUDIT and DUDIT changes in both arms and for the absence of a detectable increase in drug-use scores over about 4 months in people without current substance use disorders; it cannot be cited for an effect on alcohol use, for any population with a substance use disorder, or for long-term drug use.

key_findings.finding: Of 90 randomized and dosed in MAPP1, 82 (42 MDMA, 40 placebo) had baseline and termination AUDIT or DUDIT; none had a current alcohol use disorder; 21 (25.6%) a past alcohol use disorder, 14 (17.1%) a past substance use disorder, 2 placebo participants a current mild cannabis use disorder.

AUDIT change from baseline to study termination: −1.02 (SD 3.52) on MDMA vs +0.40 (2.70) on placebo, P = 0.0436, Hedges' g = 0.45 unadjusted; not significant after adjusting for baseline AUDIT (P = 0.52). Baseline AUDIT did not differ significantly (P = .10).
key_findings.locator: 3.2 AUDIT and DUDIT scores, 1st paragraph; Abstract › Results

key_findings.finding: Within-group AUDIT: MDMA 4.09 (4.16) at baseline and 3.24 (3.36) at termination (P = .30, g = .22); placebo 2.80 (3.18) and 3.23 (3.65) (P = .57, g = .13).
key_findings.note: These baseline means differ from Table 1 (4.26 and 2.83), and 4.09 to 3.24 is a fall of 0.85, not the printed −1.02 (reporting issues).

key_findings.finding: DUDIT change: −1.36 (3.00) on MDMA vs −0.78 (5.39) on placebo, P = 0.5452, g = 0.13 (printed 95% CI 0.013 to 0.89); within groups MDMA 2.70 (4.31) to 1.33 (3.14), placebo 3.45 (4.46) to 2.70 (6.33).
key_findings.locator: 3.2 AUDIT and DUDIT scores, 1st paragraph; Fig. 1 legend

key_findings.finding: Recall windows: AUDIT and DUDIT were given at baseline with the standard 12-month lookback and at study termination with instructions to cover the time since the end of treatment.
AUDIT change was not correlated with baseline or change in CAPS-5, BDI-II or SDS overall; in the MDMA group it correlated with baseline CAPS-5 (r = .32, P = .04; data not shown).

Limitations stated: no participant with even a mild current alcohol use disorder was recruited, although permitted; the narrow distribution of AUDIT scores limited detection of change; the exploratory, non-AUD sample limits clinical interpretation.

reporting_issues.issue: The adjusted analysis that removes the AUDIT effect (P = 0.52) is absent from the abstract and highlights, which report only the unadjusted P = 0.0436.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML (Abstract; Highlights; 3.2 AUDIT and DUDIT scores, 1st paragraph)

reporting_issues.issue: Baseline AUDIT means differ between Table 1 (4.26 and 2.83) and the Results text (4.09 and 2.80), and the text's MDMA means (4.09 to 3.24) imply a change of −0.85, not the printed −1.02; Table 1 has 42 MDMA participants although 46 minus 3 withdrawals is 43.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML (Table 1; 3.1 Sample characteristics, 1st paragraph; 3.2 AUDIT and DUDIT scores, 1st paragraph)
reporting_issues.consequence: The analysed sets for the two questionnaires may differ; the change scores cannot be reconstructed from the printed means.

reporting_issues.issue: The DUDIT effect is printed as g = 0.13 with a 95% CI of 0.013 to 0.89, an interval excluding zero for a test with P = 0.5452; F statistics are printed with their degrees of freedom reversed, as F (80, 1).
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML (3.2 AUDIT and DUDIT scores, 1st paragraph; Abstract)
reporting_issues.consequence: The DUDIT interval cannot be right; cite the P value and the change scores.

reporting_issues.issue: Table 1 arithmetic: White participants total 66 although the groups give 37 and 28 (65, which matches the printed 80.25% of 81 with race reported); past substance use disorder on placebo is 6 printed as 12.50% (6 of 40 is 15.0%); veterans 15 printed as 19.29% (15 of 82 is 18.3%). The Discussion gives a baseline DUDIT of 2.51 (3.39), range 1 to 15, which matches no figure in Table 1.
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor; the sample description has several typographical errors.

reporting_issues.issue: The Discussion cites the pooled long-term follow-up of the phase 2 trials (Jerome et al., 2020), marked retracted in PMC's reference list, for limited abuse potential in clinical settings.

verification.source_read: PMC full text PMC9750500, the accepted author manuscript (NIHMS1847922), all sections, Table 1 and figure legend, read in this reader's own browser tab; the publisher's version of record on ScienceDirect could not be opened in the app's browser and was not compared; the Crossref record for the DOI; the MAPP1 study card (sc_mitchell_2021) for the parent trial's design and registry. Fig. 1 values were not extracted.
